name: Belém Tower
desc: A little stone fortress standing in the river like it forgot the empire ended. A few euros to climb inside a postcard.

name: Jerónimos Monastery
desc: Stone carved so fine it looks piped like frosting. Sailors prayed here before sailing off the map. The church part is free.

name: Praça do Comércio
desc: A yellow royal square that opens straight onto the river. Free sunsets the size of an empire's ego.

name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
desc: The lookout locals climb at golden hour. Whole city, castle, river — free, plus whatever the guy with the cooler charges.

name: São Jorge Castle
desc: Moorish walls with peacocks on patrol. Pay up, walk the ramparts, pretend the terracotta sprawl below is all yours.

name: Tram 28
desc: A rickety yellow rollercoaster disguised as public transit. Cheapest city tour in Europe, if you can snag a seat.

name: LX Factory
desc: Old factories under the big red bridge, now bookstores, murals, and food stalls. Browsing ambition is free.

name: Oceanário de Lisboa
desc: One giant tank where sunfish drift by like slow planets. Pricey — file it under rainy-day someday splurge.

name: Santa Justa Lift
desc: A wrought-iron elevator from 1902 that hoists you over the rooftops. Or hack it: walk up the hill behind for the same view.

name: Alfama Old Town Walk
desc: Laundry-strung alleys older than the maps. Get lost on purpose; the fado leaking from doorways is free.
